title: Adjoint of a tensor-projected morphism
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be any morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ any commutative ring. Use the small ordinary etale sites and unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], inverse image $f^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], and the canonical adjunction $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$ with counit $\varepsilon_f$ as specified in [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Let $K,M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $E\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, and $a:M\to Rf_*E$. Write $a^\flat=\varepsilon_{f,E}\circ f^{-1}a:f^{-1}M\to E$ for its adjoint. Let $c_{K,M}:f^{-1}(K\otimes_A^L M)\xrightarrow{\sim}f^{-1}K\otimes_A^L f^{-1}M$ be the inverse of the canonical inverse-image tensor comparison $f^{-1}K\otimes_A^L f^{-1}M\to f^{-1}(K\otimes_A^L M)$ of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Using the canonical tensor symmetry $\sigma$ [lem-kun-tensor-sym], put
$$\pi_f(K,E)=Rf_*(\sigma)\circ\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K)\circ\sigma:
K\otimes_A^L Rf_*E\longrightarrow Rf_*(f^{-1}K\otimes_A^L E),$$
where $\mathrm{PF}$ is [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Then the adjoint of $\pi_f(K,E)\circ(1_K\otimes a)$ is
$$(1_{f^{-1}K}\otimes a^\flat)\circ c_{K,M}:
f^{-1}(K\otimes_A^L M)\longrightarrow f^{-1}K\otimes_A^L E.$$
No properness, Noetherianity, boundedness, finiteness or torsion hypothesis is imposed, and no assertion that $\pi_f(K,E)$ is invertible is made.

proof.text:
First check explicitly that the canonical comparison respects symmetry:
$$c_{V,U}\circ f^{-1}(\sigma_{U,V})=\sigma_{f^{-1}U,f^{-1}V}\circ c_{U,V}.$$
Use K-flat flat-term representatives of $U,V$. For the induced constant-coefficient ringed topoi, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] ensures that their pullbacks are K-flat flat-term representatives and that total tensors compute the derived comparison. The canonical comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] is the degreewise pullback tensor comparison on these models. The sign symmetry in [def-kun-derived-tensor], giving the canonical symmetry of [lem-kun-tensor-sym], sends a tensor in bidegree $(p,q)$ to its switched tensor times $(-1)^{pq}$. Both routes in the displayed equation therefore send the inverse image of $x\otimes y$ to $(-1)^{pq}(f^{-1}y\otimes f^{-1}x)$; bilinearity gives equality on each tensor summand and hence on the total complexes. The uniqueness of extension from K-flat flat-term models in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] gives the displayed equality for all derived objects.

proof.text:
Write $F=f^{-1}$, $R=Rf_*$ and omit tensor subscripts. By [def-kun-projection-formula-map], $\mathrm{PF}_f(E,K)$ has adjoint $(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\circ c_{RE,K}$ under the specified derived adjunction. Naturality of its Hom bijection in both arguments gives
$$\pi_f(K,E)^\flat=\sigma_{E,FK}\circ(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\circ c_{RE,K}\circ F(\sigma_{K,RE}).$$
The symmetry equation from step 1 replaces the last two factors by $\sigma_{FK,FRE}\circ c_{K,RE}$. Naturality of tensor symmetry [lem-kun-tensor-sym] then gives
$$\sigma_{E,FK}\circ(\varepsilon_E\otimes1)\circ\sigma_{FK,FRE}=1_{FK}\otimes\varepsilon_E.$$
Indeed naturality moves $\varepsilon_E$ through the second symmetry, and the two opposite switches cancel (on bidegree $(p,q)$ their sign is $(-1)^{2pq}=1$). Thus $\pi_f(K,E)^\flat=(1_{FK}\otimes\varepsilon_E)\circ c_{K,RE}$.

proof.text:
Let $h=\pi_f(K,E)\circ(1_K\otimes a)$. With the derived adjunction of [def-kun-projection-formula-map], its adjoint is $\pi_f(K,E)^\flat\circ F(1_K\otimes a)$. Explicitly this follows by expanding the adjoint as $\varepsilon\circ Fh$ and using functoriality of $F$. Bifunctoriality of the comparison in [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal] gives
$$c_{K,RE}\circ F(1_K\otimes a)=(1_{FK}\otimes Fa)\circ c_{K,M}.$$
For the inverse comparison this naturality square follows by multiplying the square for the forward comparison by its inverse components. Substituting step 2, the adjoint is therefore
$$(1_{FK}\otimes\varepsilon_E)\circ(1_{FK}\otimes Fa)\circ c_{K,M}.$$

proof.text: The derived tensor is a bifunctor on all derived morphisms by [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Its composition law rewrites the first two factors of step 3 as $1_{FK}\otimes(\varepsilon_E\circ Fa)$. The composite in parentheses is exactly $a^\flat$ by the definition of $a^\flat$ in the statement. Hence $h^\flat=(1_{FK}\otimes a^\flat)\circ c_{K,M}$, with the asserted source and target. Only the defining derived adjunction, canonical tensor comparison and bifunctor laws were used, so no projection-isomorphism, properness, boundedness or coefficient restriction is needed.
